metadata.claim_supported: Under `node12`/`nodenext`, the emitted module format for `.ts/.js` files is inferred from the nearest `package.json` `type` field, with `type: "module"` mapping to ESNext and other cases defaulting to CommonJS.
metadata.why_relevant: This matches the report that adding `type: "module"` changes whether a package can be imported.

metadata.claim_supported: NodeNext/Node12 resolution uses different condition sets for ESM versus CJS, specifically `['node','import','types']` versus `['node','require','types']`.
metadata.why_relevant: This shows why package exports can resolve differently depending on whether the importing file is treated as ESM.

metadata.claim_supported: Package.json `typings`, `types`, `main`, and `tsconfig` fields are normalized and read as path entries during module resolution.
metadata.why_relevant: This is the code that turns package metadata into candidate module entrypoints and declaration files.

metadata.claim_supported: For package resolution, JavaScript/TypeScript/DTS lookups consult different package.json fields: JS uses `main`, TypeScript uses `types`/`typings` first then `main`, and DTS-only lookups use `types`/`typings`.
metadata.why_relevant: This directly relates to a package that ships declarations versus one that relies on `@types`, and to why the declared main file matters.

metadata.claim_supported: In package resolution, `exports` has priority over file/directory lookup in NodeNext/Node12, and ESM mode otherwise falls back to `index.js` only when `main` and `exports` are absent.
metadata.coverage_area: package entrypoint lookup and ESM fallback
metadata.why_relevant: This is the control flow most likely to make a package import succeed or fail based on package metadata such as `exports`, `main`, or file extensions.
